validation.typecheck: passed: compiler, tests and all examples

change: Native Repeat Count callbacks support an optional zero-based index. Repeat and menu callbacks support local void returns, including from nested loops or switches, and awaited action returns. Each invocation has isolated return state and repeat counters.

verifiedShortcut.name: TS-Flow-Callbacks
verifiedShortcut.completion: Both runs displayed all four expected results in order and returned to the editor with play available, without an error.
verifiedShortcut.importComparison: All 112 imported actions read from the simulator database match the compiled output exactly.

nativeCoverage: Zero-based repeat indices remain independent of callback parameter mutation
Early return skips one iteration and the counter still advances
Nested repeats isolate counters and return state
Menu return from a nested for-of skips the remainder of the selected branch
Both menu branches continue after the menu
A zero-count repeat invokes no callback
compilerCoverage: Count evaluated once before callback scope, including an awaited count action
Parameter shadowing leaves outer variables unchanged
Return state resets for repeat invocations with and without an index parameter
Nested loops and switches respect callback returns; nested callbacks keep separate frames
return await action preserves effects and skipped prompts do not execute
Helpers and menu/repeat callbacks return to the correct caller
Invalid callback parameters, generic callbacks, value returns and cross-callback jumps are rejected
All prior native workflow expectations are preserved; the new fixture roundtrips through raw and catalog TypeScript
limitations: Native flow callbacks remain inline async arrows with braced bodies and void results.
No default/rest/optional index parameters, generic callbacks, function references or expression-bodied callbacks.
Runtime repeat counts should be finite integers; positive fractions retain native rounding behavior.
Local return does not break the entire repeat. Native nested loops still traverse remaining guarded iterations.
Ordinary for/while loops and complete TypeScript/Shortcuts coverage remain unfinished.
Physical devices and other OS versions were not tested.
